answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a Wesolowski VDF: a long chain of modular squarings whose next step depends on the previous result. GPUs can run separate chains in parallel, but cannot shorten any one chain through parallelism, so creating many valid identities still incurs a sequential time cost per identity. A violet marker on a mesa at dawn may illustrate the boundary: replication does not erase elapsed time.
